prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key pledges and policies (≤500 words)

Economy, tax and welfare
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and introduce an age‑related personal allowance so pension income stays below the tax‑free threshold; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
- Childcare: 30 hours free for eligible children from 9 months to school; expand wraparound care.
- Child Benefit: move to household assessment; taper between £120,000–£160,000 combined income.
- Welfare reform: tighten PIP assessments; revise Work Capability Assessment; shift fit notes to work/health professionals; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Fraud Bill; target £12bn annual savings.

Business, innovation and trade
- Maintain full expensing; consider extending to leasing; no rise in corporation tax.
- SME 10‑point plan (business rates support, prompt payment enforcement, Open Finance, regional mutual banks, targeted tax incentives).
- Public R&D to £22bn/year; invest in compute for AI; £4.5bn for strategic manufacturing; expand Catapults.
- Advance FTAs (India, GCC), implement CPTPP; uphold standards in food imports; build on UK‑EU TCA without ceding legal sovereignty.

Infrastructure and planning
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, buses, stations, potholes).
- Nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G for populated areas; support EV charging; legislate for automated vehicles.
- Speed planning approvals to one year; reform environmental assessments; limit unmerited judicial reviews.

Energy and net zero
- Net zero 2050 with “pragmatic” path: annual North Sea licensing; retain windfall tax (to 2028‑29, subject to prices); build new gas plants.
- Treble offshore wind; two CCS clusters plus further projects; scale nuclear via Great British Nuclear, approve two SMR fleets in first 100 days; new plant at Wylfa; streamline approvals; grid reforms.
- Keep green levies below 2023 levels; maintain price cap; review standing charges; £6bn for home efficiency and a universal voucher scheme; support onshore wind with local consent; solar on brownfield; fracking moratorium; introduce a carbon border adjustment by 2027.

Public services and health
- NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; 250 GP surgeries; 50 Community Diagnostic Centres; deliver 40 new hospitals by 2030.
- £3.4bn NHS tech plan (NHS App, AI diagnostics, data platform, IT upgrades); expand Pharmacy First; Martha’s Rule; Dental Recovery Plan (contract reform, service in underserved areas).
- Women’s Health strategy actions; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; Major Conditions Strategy; expand mental health support (schools to 100% coverage by 2030; early support hubs).

Education and youth
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19; mandate school‑day mobile phone bans; two hours PE weekly.
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing low‑outcome degrees; parental access to curriculum materials.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid military/cyber placements or civic service).

Borders, security and defence
- Legal annual cap on migration with annual parliamentary vote; higher work visa thresholds; pre‑travel health checks; higher visa fees and IHS; restrict dependants; expand returns deals.
- Illegal migration: implement Rwanda removals; expedite asylum processing; curb legal challenges; international asylum reform effort.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn munitions investment; increase defence R&D; long‑term Ukraine support; veterans’ legislation and benefits.

Housing and communities
- Build 1.6m homes; scrap nutrient neutrality to unlock 100,000; fast‑track brownfield in 20 biggest cities; densify inner London; protect Green Belt.
- First‑time buyers: permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425k; new Help to Buy; continue Mortgage Guarantee.
- Leasehold reform (cap ground rents); Renters Reform Bill (abolish Section 21 alongside court reform); CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; control holiday lets; tackle building safety.
- Extend UK Shared Prosperity Fund; town endowment funds; expand Freeports/Investment Zones; devolution “level 4.”

Law, order and civil liberties
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; Martyn’s Law; strengthen powers on protests; tougher sentencing (violent/sexual/domestic); build four prisons; speed courts; expand legal aid in major incidents.

Society, equality, rural and environment
- Clarify Equality Act that “sex” means biological sex; implement Cass Review; protect single‑sex facilities.
- Rural broadband, flood defence funding maintained; Plan for Water (tougher sanctions, river recovery network, regulatory reform); tree planting and urban greening; new National Park; stronger action on waste crime and DRS; limit new incinerators.

Devolution and the Union
- Protect internal market; comparable performance data across UK; direct UK funding for projects in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; sector‑specific support (energy, transport, agriculture, fisheries).
